purpose: Test whether a fixed-slot persistent representation can provide a forcing-independent hard memory bound without altering accepted topology or mass when capacity is exceeded.

topology_oracle.reference: unbounded dynamic interval list used in Gate AB topology falsification
topology_oracle.bottom_rule: physical removal on exiting the finite column

required_checks: persistent allocation is exactly constant for a fixed template and independent of run duration and forcing event count
for every accepted no-overflow trial, ordered interval coordinates equal the dynamic reference exactly
on first overflow, committed packed state is bitwise identical before and after rejected trial
on first overflow, committed mass ledger is exactly unchanged
overflow never invokes merge, clipping or water deletion
overflow emits an explicit FALLBACK_REQUIRED diagnostic
advective and explicit-diffusion variants have identical persistent topology semantics
diffusion scratch is worker-owned and excluded from persistent bytes

decision_rule.important_nonclaim: PASS proves a bounded fail-closed representation pattern only. It does not prove that eight slots are sufficient for useful FWC coverage, that 41.6 kB/column at 200 bins is acceptable, or that runtime cost is bounded under arbitrarily dense forcing events.

hard_guards: No topology approximation to avoid overflow.
No silent merge, clipping, deletion or water repair.
No physical FWC accuracy claim from this gate.
No MultiSWAP production admission from boundedness alone.
Slot count may not be retuned after execution in this gate.
Runtime event-rate boundedness remains a separate open gate even if memory boundedness passes.
